findings.root_cause: The concrete placeholder handler was changed to inherit from an abstract stateful base without implementing that base's required methods.
findings.suggested_fix: Either keep MetricAlertDetectorHandler as a concrete DetectorHandler until its stateful behavior is implemented, or implement every required StatefulDetectorHandler abstract member before assigning it to MetricAlertFire.detector_handler.
findings.title: Metric alert detector handler is now uninstantiable
findings.trigger: A Detector whose type is "metric_alert_fire" is passed to process_detectors, causing Detector.detector_handler to instantiate MetricAlertDetectorHandler.
findings.verifier_reason: Patch line R11 shows MetricAlertDetectorHandler inheriting from StatefulDetectorHandler with only 'pass' body. StatefulDetectorHandler declares abstract methods counter_names, get_dedupe_value, get_group_key_values, and build_occurrence_and_event_data (lines 143-170 in detector.py). Instantiation via Detector.detector_handler (line 86 in detector.py model) will raise TypeError for unimplemented abstract methods.

findings.verifier_reason: Patch line R177 shows data_packet with group_2 value 10, but line R191 calls build_mock_occurrence_and_event with value 6 for group_2. pr.body:
This adds a hook that can be implemented to produce an occurrence specific to the detector that is subclassing the StatefulDetector.

Also change the signature of evaluate to return a dict keyed by groupkey instead of a list. This helps avoid the chance of duplicate results for the same group key.

raw_findings.body: The producer catches the KafkaException and returns, after which process_detectors commits the queued active state and dedupe value. Subsequent packets at the same priority produce no result, so the issue occurrence is never retried and the alert is permanently lost.
raw_findings.failure_mode: Execution records the detector as active without creating the issue that represents that transition.
raw_findings.impact: The producer catches the KafkaException and returns, after which process_detectors commits the queued active state and dedupe value. Subsequent packets at the same priority produce no result, so the issue occurrence is never retried and the alert is permanently lost.
raw_findings.root_cause: The new activation occurrence is treated as successfully handled even though the publishing API suppresses Kafka failures, while state is committed unconditionally afterward.
raw_findings.suggested_fix: Make publication failure observable to process_detectors and do not commit the corresponding state update unless the occurrence has been durably accepted, for example by propagating the producer failure or using an outbox that atomically records both state and pending publication.
raw_findings.title: A failed occurrence publication still permanently advances detector state
raw_findings.trigger: A detector transitions from OK to a non-OK priority and produce_occurrence_to_kafka encounters a KafkaException while publishing the newly built occurrence.

finding.title: A failed occurrence publication still permanently advances detector state
finding.trigger: A detector transitions from OK to a non-OK priority and produce_occurrence_to_kafka encounters a KafkaException while publishing the newly built occurrence.
finding.verifier_reason: The claim that state is committed unconditionally after a KafkaException is not supported by the patch. produce_occurrence_to_kafka catches KafkaException and logs it (producer.py:82-90), but process_detectors calls commit_state_updates after the loop regardless of publication success. However, this behavior is pre-existing in the codebase, not introduced by this patch. The patch adds build_occurrence_and_event_data call but does not change the commit/exception handling flow.
